title.en: Rome Was Not Built in a Day—and Never Finished
title.sub: Every age rebuilds on the last, and the city keeps moving outward.

intro: Rome begins on a lit hilltop of eight hectares, then grows through walls, roads and rebuilding, each era setting its courses upon the last.
outro: Rome was never finished: its walls moved, its ring roads followed, and it keeps building. The same is true of your own city.

endCard.title: Rome was not built in a day. It is not finished.
endCard.sub: Every age builds again on the city before it.

eras.label: Roma Quadrata
eras.narration: Rome begins as Roma Quadrata, a small village on the Palatine above the marshes. Its founders marked out a square of ground with a plough, on ground it had already claimed.
eras.stat: Rome began as a few houses and a shrine

events.title: She-wolf of the Capitoline
events.prompt: In daylight on the Capitoline, a she-wolf figure stands in clear view against the sky

events.title: The Forum, still marsh
events.prompt: In daylight, the Forum lies as wet marshland in the valley below the Palatine, with standing water and marsh vegetation.

eras.label: The Servian Wall
eras.narration: Rome’s first wall closed a shape around its hills, turning a village into a city. Inside stood the Roman people; outside, the enemy.

events.title: The wall climbs the hill
events.prompt: Daylight view of a massive volcanic tuff wall climbing the steep Roman hill, its rough stonework following the ridge above the surrounding settlement

events.title: Seven gates, one street
events.prompt: Daylight view along a narrow ancient street leading through one of seven gateways in the volcanic tuff wall, with earth and stone buildings beyond

eras.label: The Republic spills out
eras.narration: Rome has grown far beyond its old wall, but the wall never moved; the city simply ran over it. Aqueducts bring water from the hills while the Cloaca Maxima carries the Forum valley’s filth away.
eras.stat: The wall stayed put while Rome spread beyond it

events.title: The Cloaca Maxima
events.prompt: A daylight view of the great stone drain carrying dark, muddy water through a vaulted channel beneath the Forum valley, its masonry wet and worn

events.title: Temples on the hill
events.prompt: Temples of pale stone stand on the hill in clear daylight, with the crowded city spreading far beyond the old wall across the surrounding plain

eras.label: Imperial Rome
eras.narration: Rome had about a million people, already spilling beyond the walls built later to contain it. Trajan opened the empire’s largest forum and set his column there; Hadrian rebuilt the Pantheon.
eras.stat: About one million people lived in and around Rome

events.title: Trajan's Column
events.prompt: In daylight, a tall spiral victory column rises within a vast Roman forum, its carved figures winding upward. Crowds move between stone columns and colonnaded porticoes as work continues around the monument

events.title: Pantheon Dome
events.prompt: In daylight, a vast concrete dome rests above the Pantheon's open circular portico, supported without internal columns. People enter through the broad doorway while construction continues among the surrounding city roofs

eras.label: The Aurelian Walls
eras.narration: Aurelian’s wall of fear cut through settled ground, leaving part of the old city outside. The city it enclosed was smaller than it had been a century before.

events.title: Porta Maggiore in Aurelian’s Wall
events.prompt: In daylight, a broad gateway joins the brick-faced wall as it crosses populated ground. Towers rise above nearby buildings, and people stand close to the construction line

events.title: The Pantheon, Left Outside
events.prompt: In daylight, the Pantheon stands beyond the new brick wall, surrounded by inhabited ground. The older city continues outside the enclosure while the wall forms a firm boundary across the landscape

eras.label: The wall moves out
eras.narration: The northern wall moved outward, taking the Campus Martius and the Pantheon back inside. It was the first growth in more than a century, made by moving a wall rather than building a new city.
eras.stat: First city growth in more than a century

events.title: The Pantheon, back inside
events.prompt: A daylight view across the Campus Martius toward the Pantheon, its dome rising beyond open ground and low city buildings, with the extended northern wall enclosing the surrounding landscape

events.title: A new northern line
events.prompt: Workers in period dress building a stone wall along a new northern line in daylight, with masonry, scaffolding and tools beside them and the Pantheon visible within the enlarged city

eras.label: The last Roman wall
eras.narration: By now, Rome is tiny: just a few thousand people inside a shell of empty wall. Around the Vatican, a new Roman-style wall rises, embedding ancient marble columns in its face.
eras.stat: The fourth wall, built around the Vatican

events.title: Bastione dei Cosmati
events.prompt: In daylight, the Bastione dei Cosmati joins the new Vatican wall, its massive stone face set with weathered ancient Roman marble columns beneath a clear sky

events.title: St Peter’s dome
events.prompt: In daylight, St Peter’s dome rises above the Vatican precinct, its pale curved masonry standing among the surrounding Renaissance buildings under an open sky

eras.label: Porta Pia
eras.narration: The breach at Porta Pia ended papal rule and made Rome the capital of the new kingdom of Italy. The walls came down, and their line became roads that let the city grow beyond them again.
eras.stat: Porta Pia breach ended papal rule

events.title: The breach at Porta Pia
events.prompt: A daylight view of the breached masonry at Porta Pia, with broken stones and a wide opening through the old walls beyond the gate

events.title: The wall becomes a road
events.prompt: A daylight scene of sections of the Aurelian Wall being dismantled, with workers and horses clearing stone as a broad road forms along the old wall line

eras.label: The new ring
eras.narration: Rome's newest wall is the nearly circular ring road, built in stages through farmland as districts grew around it. New metro lines and the Jubilee's rebuilding of the Tiber's banks show that work continues.
eras.stat: The ring road is Rome's third wall

events.title: The new ring road
events.prompt: A daylight view of the nearly circular ring road crossing the Agro Romano, with construction crews, bare soil and new roadbed at its edge. Small districts begin gathering along the route while the older city remains in the distance

events.title: Metro C at the Colosseum
events.prompt: A daylight street scene beside the Colosseum, with Metro C construction exposed below the pavement, workers among concrete tunnel sections and earthworks. Beyond, bridge piers rise near the Tiber as the river banks are rebuilt
